# Block 9: Functionalise a script step and prove the result is unchanged {.unnumbered} By the end of this block you can let an agent turn working code into a function and prove that nothing changed. The proof is a characterisation testA test that checks new code reproduces the saved output of the original code exactly. It shows the output is unchanged, not that it is correct., as in the [tidy-evaluation chapter](05-tidy-evaluation.qmd): you freeze the original output, and the new code must reproduce it exactly. One request to a shipped skill does the work in order: take the snapshot, refactor, write the test. It stops twice for you: once to commit the snapshot before any code changes, and once to read the diff. This block follows [the safe vibe-coding recipe](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd#safe-recipe): the protections and checks are in place, so your part is one request, one commit, one read of the diff and one test run. *⏱ ~35 minutes* :::{.callout-important} ## Where this fits: same repository, back to the original data You keep working in the **same workshop repository**, with the `AGENTS.md` from Block 5 and the deny rules from Block 6. This block goes back to `data/raw/voles_metabolism.csv`, the data you explored in Block 4, **not** Block 7's cleaned file. Block 7's tests stay in `tests/` and run with everything else: they pass if you finished Block 7 and skip if you did not. **Start state:** `main` with your Block 7 work committed, or the `block7-done` branch. Every file you need is already in the repository; nothing needs downloading. ::: ### Files for this block {#block9-files} **Shipped with the template, used in earlier blocks.** | File | First used | Its job here | |---|---|---| | `data/raw/voles_metabolism.csv` | Block 2 | The data being summarised | | `scripts/functions/load_voles.R` | Block 4 (through `explore_voles.R`) | Reads the data with fixed column types | | `tests/test_controls.R` | Blocks 5 and 6 | Now also checks that you protected the new test | | Deny rules `Edit(/tests/fixtures/**)` and `Edit(/tests/make_reference.R)` in `.claude/settings.json` | Block 6 | Keep the agent's edit tools off the reference and its capture script | **Shipped with the template, first used here.** You read these; you do not write them. | File | Written by | Its job | |---|---|---| | `scripts/05_analysis.R`, `scripts/04_load_data.R` | Course team | The original, trusted analysis you will refactor, and the loading step it calls | | `tests/make_reference.R` | Course team | The capture script: saves the original output as the reference | | `tests/test_reference_guard.R` | Course team | Checks the agent's test reads your reference, and the reference is unchanged since you committed it | | `.agents/skills/characterisation-refactor/` (and its copy in `.claude/skills/`) | Course team | The procedure: capture, refactor, test, in that order | **Created in this block.** | File | Created by | Step | |---|---|---| | `tests/fixtures/metabolic_summary.rds` | The skill runs `make_reference.R`; **you** commit it | 1 | | `scripts/functions/summary_functions.R`; changes to `scripts/05_analysis.R` | The agent | 1 | | `tests/test_summary_functions.R` | The agent | 1 | | `Edit(/tests/test_summary_functions.R)` deny rule (saved in `.claude/settings.local.json` or `settings.json`) | You, with `/permissions` | 1 | | `tests/test_known_answers.R`; changes to `summary_functions.R` | The agent | 2 | | The re-captured reference | You | 2 | Short of time at any step? The `block9-done` branch has both steps done. ## The code you will refactor `scripts/05_analysis.R` loads the trial data and summarises post-treatment metabolic rate (mean, SD and count) by treatment arm and sex. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Reference: the code you will refactor ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # scripts/05_analysis.R: the original, trusted version ---- library(tidyverse) library(here) source(here("scripts", "04_load_data.R")) metabolic_summary <- voles |> group_by(treatment_arm, sex) |> summarise( mean_rate = mean(metabolic_rate_post), sd_rate = sd(metabolic_rate_post), n = n(), .groups = "drop" ) ``` ::: ::: :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## The data loading it relies on ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # scripts/04_load_data.R ---- library(tidyverse) library(here) source(here("scripts", "functions", "load_voles.R")) voles <- load_voles() ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # scripts/functions/load_voles.R ---- load_voles <- function() { readr::read_csv( here::here("data", "raw", "voles_metabolism.csv"), col_types = readr::cols( subject_id = readr::col_character(), sex = readr::col_character(), treatment_arm = readr::col_character(), mass_pre_g = readr::col_double(), mass_post_g = readr::col_double(), metabolic_rate_post = readr::col_double() ) ) } ``` ::: ::: One thing to notice and leave alone: the data have one missing `metabolic_rate_post`, and there is no `na.rm`, so one cell of the result is `NA`. Step 2 is about exactly this. The whole block in one picture: the reference comes from the original code, you commit it before anything changes, and from then on only a decision of yours replaces it. ::::::: {.dia .dia-lanes role="figure" aria-label="The characterisation-test loop. Step 1, refactor without changing the output: the skill runs your shipped make_reference.R on the original code; you commit the reference; the skill refactors only; you read the diff; the skill writes a test that reads your reference; you protect the new test with /permissions; the test suite passes in a fresh R session. Step 2, when the behaviour should change: you decide the output is wrong; the agent changes the function; the characterisation test fails, correctly; the known-answer test passes; you re-capture, with a commit message saying why. Nothing regenerates the reference once you have committed it, except your own recorded decision."} :::::: {.dia-flow} ::: {.dia-label} Step 1: refactor without changing the output ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-ai} Skill: run `make_reference.R` on the original code ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-you} Commit the reference ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-ai} Skill: refactor only ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-you} Read the diff ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-ai} Skill: a test that reads your reference ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-you} Protect the new test (`/permissions`) ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-check} The test suite passes in a fresh R session ::: :::::: :::::: {.dia-flow} ::: {.dia-label} Step 2: when the behaviour should change ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-you} Decide the output is wrong ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-ai} Change the function ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-check} Characterisation test fails, correctly ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-check} Known-answer test passes ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-you} Re-capture, with a commit message saying why ::: :::::: ::: {.dia-caption} A reference made after the code changed is produced by the code under test, and can only confirm that the code agrees with itself. Committing it first is what makes it a reference. ::: ::::::: ## Step 0: check the protections {#step-0} :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Recipe check (3 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Start state:** your workshop project open in RStudio or Positron, the Git pane showing no changes, on `main` (or `block7-done`). **1. Check the protections.** Start `claude` in the Terminal tab and type `/permissions`. The deny rulesA permission rule in the deny list of .claude/settings.json that stops Claude Code’s built-in tools from editing or reading the matching files. It checks shell output redirects such as > file, but not R code or most other commands that change the same files. `Edit(/tests/fixtures/**)` and `Edit(/tests/make_reference.R)` keep the agent's edit tools away from the reference and its capture script; the Git pane shows a change by any other route. **2. Check there is no reference yet.** `tests/fixtures/` holds only `raw_checksum.txt` (Block 7). The reference does not exist until Step 1 captures it. **You are done when** you have seen the two rules, and `tests/fixtures/` has no `.rds` file. **If it goes wrong:** if you are far behind, switch to the `block9-done` branch from the Git pane's branch menu and read on. :::: ::: :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## The shipped capture script, `tests/make_reference.R` It runs the original `05_analysis.R` and saves the result. The course team wrote it; a deny rule stops the agent editing it. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # tests/make_reference.R ---- # Run ONCE, by you, BEFORE any refactoring. source(here::here("scripts", "05_analysis.R")) dir.create(here::here("tests", "fixtures"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE) saveRDS( metabolic_summary, here::here("tests", "fixtures", "metabolic_summary.rds") ) ``` ::: ::: ## Step 1: snapshot, refactor and test with the skill {#step-1} The shipped skillA folder containing a SKILL.md file (and optionally scripts and templates) that an assistant loads only when it is invoked by name or judged relevant from its description. `characterisation-refactor` (`/skills` lists it) carries every rule you would otherwise type, and works in order: 1. **Snapshot.** It runs your `make_reference.R` on the original code, then stops for you to commit the result. It runs the script only if no reference exists yet and `scripts/` has no uncommitted changes. 2. **Refactor only**, then stop for your diff review. 3. **Test**: a test that reads **your** committed reference. Who runs the capture script matters less than *when*: before any code changes, from a script you trust, and committed by you. After that, git and `test_reference_guard.R` notice any change to the reference. :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## `characterisation-refactor/SKILL.md` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` markdown --- name: characterisation-refactor description: >- Refactors working R analysis code into documented functions under a characterisation test, so the output is proved unchanged. Use when asked to functionalise, refactor or tidy a script whose output must not change. Not for fixing bugs or changing results. disable-model-invocation: true --- # Refactor under a characterisation test ## The reference comes from the original code, and the user commits it The frozen reference in tests/fixtures/ is written by the user's own capture script (tests/make_reference.R) from the original, unchanged code, and the user commits it before anything else changes. A reference made after the code has changed proves nothing. - Run tests/make_reference.R at most once, in step 2 below, and only if no reference exists yet and git status shows no uncommitted changes under scripts/. Never run it at any other time, and never edit the capture script. - Never edit, regenerate or delete anything under tests/fixtures/. - If a reference already exists, use it as it is. ## Procedure 1. Present a plan: whether a reference must be captured, the code to move, the function name and file, and the test file. Wait for the user to confirm. 2. Capture only, if no reference exists. Run git status; if anything under scripts/ has uncommitted changes, stop and ask. Otherwise run Rscript tests/make_reference.R, report the file it wrote, and stop: ask the user to commit it before you change any code. Do not commit it yourself. 3. Refactor only. Write the function in scripts/functions/ with a roxygen2 block and an argument check, and make the original script call it. Do not write or edit tests in this step. Stop and let the user review the diff. 4. Test only. Write tests/test_.R (for scripts/functions/summary_functions.R, that is tests/test_summary_functions.R). Start it with library(testthat) and testthat::local_edition(3), source the function files with here::here(), read the reference from tests/fixtures/ with readRDS(), and compare it with the function's output using expect_equal(). Never hard-code expected values, and never reimplement the computation inside the test. Include an expect_error() test showing that the argument check rejects data with a required column missing. 5. Run every test in a fresh R session, Rscript -e "testthat::test_dir('tests')", and report the output verbatim, including skips. ## Rules - If the test fails, report the difference. Never change the test, the tolerance or the reference to make it pass. - Sort the output rows explicitly with dplyr::arrange() on the grouping columns, so the order never depends on how the data happen to be stored. - Do not change behaviour, including how missing values are handled. A passing test shows the output is unchanged, not that it is correct; list anything that looks wrong for the user to decide. ``` ::: ::: ::: :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} One request, one commit, one diff, one test run (20 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Start state:** Step 0 done, the Git pane clean, and Claude Code running in Manual mode in the Terminal tab (`/clear` if an earlier conversation is still open). **1. Ask.** **Prompt (Claude Code):** ```text /characterisation-refactor Move the summary in scripts/05_analysis.R into summarise_metabolic_rate() in scripts/functions/summary_functions.R. ``` Read its plan: it should say it will capture the reference first. Choose **"Yes, manually approve edits"**, and read each request before approving it. **2. Commit the reference when it stops.** The only new file in the Git pane should be `tests/fixtures/metabolic_summary.rds`. Commit it with the message "Capture reference output before refactoring", then tell the agent to carry on. **3. Read the diff when it stops again.** Select each changed file in the Git pane and choose **Diff**, then tell it to carry on and write the test. **4. Protect the new test.** Type `/permissions` and add the deny rule `Edit(/tests/test_summary_functions.R)`. It takes effect at once, and from now on new tests go in new files. **5. Run the checks.** Restart R (*Session → Restart R*), then in the R console: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} testthat::test_dir(here::here("tests")) ``` ::: | Test | Passing proves | |---|---| | `test_summary_functions.R` (written by the agent in this step) | the function reproduces your reference exactly | | `test_reference_guard.R` (shipped) | the agent's test reads your reference rather than typing numbers, and the reference is unchanged since you committed it | | `test_controls.R` (shipped, from Block 5) | every deny rule is in place, including the new one | The other blocks' tests run too; they pass, or skip if you did not do that block. **You are done when** the suite has no failures and the Git pane shows only the function, `05_analysis.R` and the new test as changed. Commit them. **If it goes wrong:** - **The capture.** If the agent declines to run `make_reference.R`, or a guard hook from Block 6 blocks it, capture it yourself: restart R, run `source(here::here("tests", "make_reference.R"))`, commit the `.rds`, and tell the agent the reference is committed. - **Changed files.** If anything other than the `.rds` changed before your commit, **Revert** it and ask again. - **Row order.** A failure on row order, not values, means the function used `.by` without sorting: ask the agent to add `dplyr::arrange(treatment_arm, sex)`. - **The new rule.** If `test_controls.R` says the test is unprotected, check the rule's spelling in `/permissions`. Otherwise, **Revert** the agent's files and ask again, or switch to `block9-done`. **Payoff.** What did the agent do, how long did checking it take, and would you automate this again? :::: ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Using Posit Assistant Posit Assistant reads the same skill from `.agents/skills/`. Use it in Normal mode and run the same test suite; with no path rules for edits, the Git pane and `test_reference_guard.R` are what protect the reference. ::: ## Step 2: unchanged is not correct {#step-2} Your test passes, **including the `NA` cell**: the refactor faithfully kept a missing mean for one group. If you wanted the mean of the animals that were measured, the original code was wrong all along. A characterisation test cannot tell, because it compares against the past, not against the truth. :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Decide, change, and test the change independently (12 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **1. Decide.** The mean and standard deviation should use measured animals only, and the count should not include the unmeasured animal (`n()` counts rows). **2. Ask for the change and a known-answer test.** **Prompt (Claude Code):** ```text Handle missing metabolic_rate_post values in summarise_metabolic_rate(): mean and SD with na.rm = TRUE, and add n_used and n_missing instead of n. Put a known-answer test on a small tibble in a new file, tests/test_known_answers.R, and show me the expected values and how you worked them out. Do not change tests/test_summary_functions.R. ``` A known-answer testA test that checks code against a result worked out independently, for example by hand. It can show code is correct, where a characterisation test only shows it is unchanged. checks the new behaviour against a result you can work out by hand. **Check the arithmetic yourself**: the mean of 10, 14 and a missing value is 12, from two measured animals and one missing.
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # scripts/functions/summary_functions.R: missing values handled ---- summarise_metabolic_rate <- function(data) { stopifnot(is.data.frame(data)) required <- c("treatment_arm", "sex", "metabolic_rate_post") missing_cols <- setdiff(required, names(data)) if (length(missing_cols) > 0) { stop( "`data` is missing required column(s): ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE ) } data |> dplyr::summarise( mean_rate = mean(metabolic_rate_post, na.rm = TRUE), sd_rate = stats::sd(metabolic_rate_post, na.rm = TRUE), n_used = sum(!is.na(metabolic_rate_post)), n_missing = sum(is.na(metabolic_rate_post)), .by = c(treatment_arm, sex) ) |> dplyr::arrange(treatment_arm, sex) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # tests/test_known_answers.R ---- library(testthat) testthat::local_edition(3) source(here::here("scripts", "functions", "summary_functions.R")) test_that("means ignore missing values and n_used counts measured animals", { toy_df <- tibble::tibble( treatment_arm = c("Control", "Control", "Control"), sex = c("F", "F", "F"), metabolic_rate_post = c(10, 14, NA) ) result <- summarise_metabolic_rate(toy_df) expect_equal(result$mean_rate, 12) expect_equal(result$n_used, 2) expect_equal(result$n_missing, 1) }) ``` :::
**3. Watch the characterisation test fail, correctly.** Run the suite as in Step 1: the output has changed, and the test tells you so. The known-answer test passes. **4. Re-capture the reference, as a recorded decision.** This one is yours, not the skill's: the skill only captures a reference that does not exist yet. Restart R, then in the R console: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} source(here::here("tests", "make_reference.R")) ``` ::: **5. Commit, then run the suite.** Commit the reference, the function and the new test file with a message that says why, for example "Exclude missing metabolic rates from mean and SD; report n_used and n_missing". Only then run the suite as in Step 1. The order matters: until the new reference is committed, `test_reference_guard.R` fails, because git reports uncommitted changes under `tests/fixtures/`. Re-capturing is safe here for three reasons: you decided it, a known-answer test checks the new behaviour, and the commit records why. **You are done when** the whole suite passes again and the re-captured reference is committed with its reason. **If it goes wrong:** if the known-answer test fails, the arithmetic or the function is wrong; read both before changing either. If time is short, switch to the `block9-done` branch, which has Step 2 done. :::: ::: The general rule: characterisation tests protect behaviour you have already judged correct. Judging it correct is a separate step, and it is yours. :::{.callout-note} ## Check · Reproduce · Record - **You can now:** let an agent snapshot, refactor and test working analysis code with one request, **trusted because** the reference came from the original code and you committed it before anything changed, and a shipped guard test proves the agent's test uses it. - **Check:** the whole test suite; the diff in the Git pane; the arithmetic of the known-answer test. - **Reproduce:** the suite passes after *Session → Restart R*, with nothing changed under `tests/fixtures/`. - **Record:** the re-captured reference is a decision with a commit message that says why. Add a line to `docs/ai-log.md`: the request, whether the test passed first time, and what you changed. ::: ## Check your understanding **A characterisation test passes after a refactor. What has it established?**
**Why must the reference be captured and committed before the refactor starts?**
**The shipped deny rules protect tests/fixtures/ in Claude Code. Once you have committed the reference, which action could still change it?**
## Going further (not covered live) {#going-further} This material is not covered in the live session. Work through it afterwards if it is useful to you. ::::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## What the skill does, step by step The skill turns a capture and two prompts into one request. Written out by hand, the capture is yours: restart R, run `source(here::here("tests", "make_reference.R"))`, and commit the `.rds`. The two prompts are below. Splitting the work matters: a single prompt that writes both the refactor and the test lets one misunderstanding (about row order, say) shape both files at once, producing a passing test that proves nothing. **Prompt 1: the refactor only.** ```text Move the computation in scripts/05_analysis.R into a documented function summarise_metabolic_rate() in scripts/functions/summary_functions.R, with a roxygen2 block and an argument check. Make 05_analysis.R call the new function instead of the inline pipeline. Do not write any tests, and do not touch anything under tests/. ``` **Prompt 2: the test only.** ```text Add tests/test_summary_functions.R. It must call local_edition(3), source scripts/functions/load_voles.R and scripts/functions/summary_functions.R, read tests/fixtures/metabolic_summary.rds, and compare it with summarise_metabolic_rate(load_voles()) using expect_equal(). Do not create, regenerate or modify anything under tests/fixtures/, and do not run tests/make_reference.R. I captured that reference myself; a reference you generate proves nothing. ``` Before trusting a passing test you would check four things: the test reads the `.rds` rather than hard-coding numbers; it calls the function rather than reimplementing the pipeline; nothing changed under `tests/fixtures/`; and the agent's commands (shown in the conversation) include no run of `tests/make_reference.R` after the capture you committed. The shipped `test_reference_guard.R` now checks the first three automatically; the fourth is why you read approval requests in Manual mode. :::{.callout-warning} **What a deny rule does not cover.** Claude Code's deny rules apply to its built-in file tools, and to shell output redirects such as `> file`, but not to R code or most other commands it runs. The skill relies on that to take the first snapshot; an agent that ran `Rscript tests/make_reference.R` again later would overwrite your reference without touching an edit tool. That is why git, and `test_reference_guard.R`, are the final checks. ::: To use the skill in your own projects, download it and unzip it into your project's `.agents/skills/` (and copy it into `.claude/skills/` for Claude Code): ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: :::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Without an agent: write the function and the test yourself Everything here is written by you; only `make_reference.R` and the data are shipped. First capture and commit the reference as above. A tidy refactor naturally reaches for the modern `.by` argument. Write this first attempt in a new file, `scripts/functions/summary_functions.R`:
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # scripts/functions/summary_functions.R: first attempt ---- summarise_metabolic_rate <- function(data) { data |> dplyr::summarise( mean_rate = mean(metabolic_rate_post), sd_rate = stats::sd(metabolic_rate_post), n = dplyr::n(), .by = c(treatment_arm, sex) ) } ``` :::
Now write the test and run it: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # tests/test_summary_functions.R ---- library(testthat) local_edition(3) source(here::here("scripts", "functions", "load_voles.R")) source(here::here("scripts", "functions", "summary_functions.R")) test_that("summarise_metabolic_rate() reproduces the original summary", { reference <- readRDS(here::here("tests", "fixtures", "metabolic_summary.rds")) expect_equal(summarise_metabolic_rate(load_voles()), reference, tolerance = 1e-8) }) ``` ::: Run it with `testthat::test_file(here::here("tests", "test_summary_functions.R"))`.
It fails, and not on the numbers. `.by` returns the groups in order of first appearance; the reference, made with `group_by()`, has them sorted. The values are right but the rows are in a different order, and `expect_equal()` reports a mismatch. Add `dplyr::arrange(treatment_arm, sex)` to the end of the pipeline and the test passes. That failure is the lesson in miniature: a change that improved the code altered the output, and the characterisation test caught it. If your test passed first time, the data happen to be stored in sorted order. Check with `load_voles() |> dplyr::distinct(treatment_arm, sex)`.
Do not type the expected numbers into the test as literals: a test that compares the function with numbers you transcribed proves nothing about whether the refactor preserved the original computation. The test must *read the `.rds`*.
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # scripts/functions/summary_functions.R: refactored ---- #' Summarise post-treatment metabolic rate by treatment arm and sex #' #' @param data A data frame with columns treatment_arm, sex and #' metabolic_rate_post. #' @return A tibble with one row per treatment_arm and sex, sorted by both, #' giving the mean, standard deviation and number of rows. summarise_metabolic_rate <- function(data) { stopifnot(is.data.frame(data)) required <- c("treatment_arm", "sex", "metabolic_rate_post") missing_cols <- setdiff(required, names(data)) if (length(missing_cols) > 0) { stop( "`data` is missing required column(s): ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE ) } data |> dplyr::summarise( mean_rate = mean(metabolic_rate_post), sd_rate = stats::sd(metabolic_rate_post), n = dplyr::n(), .by = c(treatment_arm, sex) ) |> dplyr::arrange(treatment_arm, sex) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # scripts/05_analysis.R: after refactoring ---- library(tidyverse) library(here) source(here("scripts", "04_load_data.R")) source(here("scripts", "functions", "summary_functions.R")) metabolic_summary <- summarise_metabolic_rate(voles) ``` :::
::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Protecting the new test by editing the settings file `/permissions` is the simple route. The same rule can be added by hand: open `.claude/settings.json` in the editor and add `"Edit(/tests/test_summary_functions.R)"` to the `deny` list, minding the comma after the line before. Claude Code reloads the file without a restart. `test_controls.R` checks the result either way. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## The review gate Local controls do not exist for an agent that works remotely. On GitHub, a pull request that changes a file under `tests/` can be held until the code owner reviews it. How to set up CODEOWNERS and branch protection is in the *Going further* section of [Block 6](11f-enforced-controls.qmd). ::: :::::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Reuse the skill on a second step A skill earns its keep the second time you use it. :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Reuse the skill (15 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **1. Capture a reference yourself first.** Pick a second step: the plotting code in `scripts/explore_mass_change_plot.R`, which you made in [Block 4](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd) (it is on `block5-done` if you need it), or a step from your own project. The skill runs only the shipped `make_reference.R`, so for any other step the capture is yours: write a small capture script modelled on it, run it after restarting R, commit its output in `tests/fixtures/`, and protect the script with `/permissions`. **2. Invoke the skill.** **Prompt (Claude Code):** ```text /characterisation-refactor Functionalise the step in scripts/explore_mass_change_plot.R that I captured in tests/fixtures/. Start with the plan. ``` **3. Compare.** Did the agent still stop between the refactor and the test? Run the whole suite, and check the Git pane for anything changed under `tests/fixtures/`. :::: ::: ::::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## An asynchronous agent: the Copilot cloud agent The same work can be handed to an agent that runs remotely while you do something else. It works on a branch in GitHub's infrastructure and returns a pull request. Before you start, check that your Copilot plan includes the cloud agent, that `copilot-setup-steps.yml` is on your default branch (see *The environment the test runs in* below), and that the repository is protected. **Protect the reference on GitHub.** Local deny rules do not exist for a remote agent. Add a `.github/CODEOWNERS` file naming yourself for the protected paths, and turn on branch protection for `main` so that merging requires your review and a passing `r-checks` run: ``` /tests/fixtures/ @your-github-username /tests/make_reference.R @your-github-username /.github/ @your-github-username ``` Keep the two-step discipline by writing **two issues**, and assign the second only after you have reviewed and merged the first. **Issue 1** ```text Title: Move the metabolic-rate summary into a function Move the summary computation in scripts/05_analysis.R into a documented function summarise_metabolic_rate() in scripts/functions/summary_functions.R, with a roxygen2 block and an argument check. Make 05_analysis.R call it. Acceptance criteria: - Do not add or change anything under tests/, data/ or .github/. - The output must be identical to the current output, including row order and the existing NA value. ``` **Issue 2 (after Issue 1 is merged)** ```text Title: Add a characterisation test for summarise_metabolic_rate() Add tests/test_summary_functions.R. It must call local_edition(3), source scripts/functions/load_voles.R and scripts/functions/summary_functions.R, and compare summarise_metabolic_rate(load_voles()) with tests/fixtures/metabolic_summary.rds using expect_equal(). Acceptance criteria: - Do not create, modify or regenerate anything under tests/fixtures/, and do not run tests/make_reference.R. - Run the tests and report the result in the pull request description. ``` Assign each issue to Copilot. When a pull request arrives: 1. Open **Files changed**. Confirm that only the expected files changed. A change under `tests/fixtures/` or `.github/` should not merge, and CODEOWNERS will in any case require your review for it. 2. Read the test against the four checks in *What the skill does, step by step* above, or run `test_reference_guard.R`. 3. Check that the `r-checks` run on the pull request passed. 4. Pull the branch and run the test on your own machine. The agent's report that "tests pass" is its claim; your run is the check. If something is wrong, comment on the pull request to ask for a revision, or close it. Nothing reaches `main` until you merge. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## The environment the test runs in A characterisation test is only as stable as the environment it runs in. The column types in `load_voles()` handle the finest-grained part. The R version and the package set are handled by two GitHub Actions workflows. Neither ships with the template: to use them, create each file in `.github/workflows/`. `r-checks.yml` is the independent check. It runs the tests from a clean checkout on every push to `main` and on every pull request: ```yaml name: r-checks on: push: branches: [main] pull_request: jobs: tests: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2 with: r-version: "4.5.2" # match the R version in renv.lock use-public-rspm: true - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2 - name: Run tests run: Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("tests", stop_on_failure = TRUE)' ``` It is independent of your machine and of the agent's environment, but it is not tamper-proof. A pull request can change the workflow file or the reference it checks against. CODEOWNERS and branch protection (above) are what make a passing run meaningful: you review every change to those paths before it merges. `copilot-setup-steps.yml` builds the environment the Copilot cloud agent works in. Following GitHub's documented pattern: ```yaml name: "Copilot Setup Steps" # Runs when this file changes, so you can see whether setup succeeds, # and can be run by hand from the Actions tab. on: workflow_dispatch: push: paths: - .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml pull_request: paths: - .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml jobs: # The job must be called copilot-setup-steps or Copilot will not use it. copilot-setup-steps: runs-on: ubuntu-latest permissions: contents: read steps: - name: Check out repository uses: actions/checkout@v4 - name: Set up R uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2 with: r-version: "4.5.2" # match the R version in renv.lock use-public-rspm: true - name: Restore packages from renv.lock uses: r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2 ``` Four requirements, each with a different failure mode: - **The job name must be exactly `copilot-setup-steps`.** If it is not, Copilot ignores the file and works without your packages. That failure is usually loud: the tests error on the first missing function. - **The file must be on the default branch**, or it is not used. - **The runner must be Ubuntu x64 Linux or Windows 64-bit.** The cloud agent does not support macOS runners; Ubuntu is the usual choice for R. - **The lockfile must be restored.** If it restores the wrong versions, the failure is quiet: tests run and pass against different package behaviour. The frozen reference then certifies sameness against the wrong baseline. When the agent's test run and the independent `r-checks` run disagree, suspect the environment before you suspect the code. ::: ## Glossary ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
term definition
characterisation test A test that checks new code reproduces the saved output of the original code exactly. It shows the output is unchanged, not that it is correct.
deny rule A permission rule in the deny list of .claude/settings.json that stops Claude Code's built-in tools from editing or reading the matching files. It checks shell output redirects such as > file, but not R code or most other commands that change the same files.
known-answer test A test that checks code against a result worked out independently, for example by hand. It can show code is correct, where a characterisation test only shows it is unchanged.
skill A folder containing a SKILL.md file (and optionally scripts and templates) that an assistant loads only when it is invoked by name or judged relevant from its description.
````` ::: ::: ## References - GitHub documentation: *Configure the development environment* (Copilot cloud agent, `copilot-setup-steps.yml`), ; *About code owners*, . - r-lib/actions: *GitHub Actions for the R community*, .
